chaining: 192 H100-hours for one weekend is the densest short-lived allocation, and it composes with the $100 Prime Intellect credits because those can be spent after the event on the same model code. What it does not do is leave anything behind: the event ends, the machines go back, and the project must be runnable on rented hardware afterwards.

notes: Included as the clearest example of the shape that recurs: eight accelerators for a weekend, awarded to everyone who attends rather than to a winner. The arithmetic is 8 x 24 = 192 GPU-hours per team, and the event is dated by the Devpost listing rather than by a date sentence on the page, so the expiry of this instance is inferred from the listing rather than documented. Three explanations for why sponsors fund this were considered: model adoption, recruiting, and eval supply. The page names four sponsors across three track themes, which fits adoption and recruiting better than any research purpose.
